_readme: THE MONITOR REGISTER — [pipeline E-9] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/11-measurement.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
Every hostname this factory serves, and whether anything is watching it.
WHY IT EXISTS. E-9's acceptance is 'every live hostname has a monitor, and the list cannot silently
shrink'. Until this file landed the right-hand side did not exist: the monitor set lived only inside
GlitchTip on the Oracle box, and the comparison the acceptance names was performed by a human, from
memory, when someone happened to look. Measured 2026-08-01 and again 2026-08-02: six monitors, five
hostnames, and TWO deployed custom domains — platform.nikatru.com and config.nikatru.com — that
nothing watches, both of them bound in services/platform/wrangler.jsonc since the day the Worker
shipped. Nobody had decided not to monitor them. Nobody had noticed.
🔴 THE HOSTNAME LIST IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED. tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs computes the
deployed set from the tree on every run — Worker custom domains, the app catalogue, and each site's
own canonical URL — and fails when a hostname the repo deploys has no row here. That is the half a
hand-written list can never have: adding a route to a wrangler.jsonc acquires a monitoring
obligation the moment it merges, rather than when somebody remembers this file exists.
⚠️ AND THE CHECK IS DELIBERATELY SPLIT IN TWO.
· tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs   OFFLINE. Runs in ci.yml, reads only the tree, needs no
token and no network. Fails on an undeclared deployed hostname or a dead row.
· tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs          LIVE, AND IT IS A SCHEDULED CI JOB — NOT the hand-run
command this bullet used to call it. OWNER_QUEUE S-8 CLOSED at 2026-08-11T16:55:34Z when
GLITCHTIP_TOKEN became a repository secret (tooling/channel-register.json:813), and
.github/workflows/ops-watch.yml:456 has run it unattended ever since, in the `glitchtip` job, on
FOUR schedules — 07:30, 08:50 and 19:30 UTC daily plus 07:45 UTC Mondays — and on
workflow_dispatch. ⚠️ The script's OWN header still reads 'NOT RUN BY CI, AND THAT IS THE
DESIGN' at tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs:28-34. That header is STALE, and it is not this
file's to fix.
🔴 AND ITS RED IS NOT A CONSOLE MESSAGE — KNOW THE BLAST RADIUS BEFORE EDITING A ROW. It exits
1 on drift, which fails the `glitchtip` job, and ops-watch.yml:525-527 is
`needs: [heartbeats, status, supabase-drift, prod-provenance, runner-budget, glitchtip]` with
`if: failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule'`, whose step opens or comments the
portfolio's SINGLE DURABLE ALERT ISSUE, title 'Scheduled duty is not reporting healthy' —
reused for every later failure and explicitly NEVER closed automatically. So a row here that
describes a monitor the live instance does not have costs a human's attention until that human
closes the issue by hand.
⚠️ THEREFORE A ROW AND ITS LIVE MONITOR ARE ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO. Declaring an `expectedBody`
here before the GlitchTip PUT lands is the SAME DEFECT as a monitor that cannot see a fault,
pointed the other way: a record claiming coverage that does not exist.
· tooling/ops/verify-alarm-chains.mjs      LIVE, and a DIFFERENT question. Everything above asks
'is this host watched'. That asks 'and if the watcher goes red, does a human find out' — the
question nothing was asking while monitor id 6 sat with project_id = NULL, unable to notify
anyone, going Down 13 times of 41 checks. verify-monitors.mjs prints that same monitor as
'not filed under any hostname', correctly and reassuringly, and cannot see the defect. A host
can be fully covered here and still be silent.
That split is why the OFFLINE guard, and only the offline guard, runs on every push: a per-push
limb needing a network token would either be skipped — and a skipped check is a check that reports
ok — or it would make every build depend on the Oracle box, which is the exact single point of
failure the observability note below is about. The live half answers that by running on a SCHEDULE
and gating no merge. But it IS automated and its red IS durable, so read the bullet above before
you edit a row: nothing in this stage is run by hand any more.
⚠️ `monitor: null` IS A GAP, NOT A WAIVER. Those rows are PRINTED on every guard run and never fail
the build. A guard that failed CI on a gap would block every branch on work that is not a change to
this repository. Printing is what stops the gap becoming invisible instead.
🔴 BUT THE REASON THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO GIVE WAS WRONG, AND IT PARKED THE TWO HIGHEST-CONSEQUENCE
GAPS IN THE TREE FOR THREE DAYS. It said creating a monitor is 'an action on the owner's GlitchTip
instance rather than a change to this repository', and both gap rows repeated it as 'An owner action'.
It is not: the GlitchTip API takes the vault GLITCHTIP_TOKEN and creates monitors, and on 2026-08-05
an agent did exactly that — twice as throwaways while proving the alert chain, then for real, closing
platform.nikatru.com and config.nikatru.com. Same shape as 'the agent sandbox cannot SSH out', which
survived in four files and parked a whole hardening backlog behind a constraint already disproved.
PROBE A DOCUMENTED LIMIT BEFORE INHERITING IT — and note that BOTH of these were owner-gated in
writing while being fully agent-doable, so the phrase 'owner action' in this file is a claim that
needs evidence, not a category.
⚠️ The gap rows that were closed are kept as `closedGap`, not deleted. A register that erases its
own gaps on closing cannot answer 'how long was this open, and why' — which is the only question
that would have caught the false reason above.
[14]O-2 must CONSUME this register rather than re-enumerate the hostnames. Two enumerations of one
list is how the ceiling budget came to disagree with itself by 5x.

_derivation.workerCustomDomains: every routes[] entry with custom_domain: true across services/*/wrangler.jsonc
_derivation.appCatalogue: every url and api host in catalog/apps.json
_derivation.siteCanonicals: the <link rel="canonical"> host of each sites/*/index.html (_shared is not a site)
declared: A hostname NO deploy config can mention, because it is the thing doing the watching.
Exactly one row may carry role: "observability", and the guard requires that row to exist —
otherwise 'is the monitor host itself monitored' is a question nothing in the tree asks.
⚠️ WIDENED 2026-09-03, AND THE WIDENING IS BOUNDED BY A RULE RATHER THAN BY A COUNT. Until that
day `declared` held exactly one row — glitchtip.nikatru.com, the watcher. It now also holds
api-auth.nikatru.com and studio.nikatru.com, the self-hosted Supabase stack whose monitors
first appeared on the instance on 2026-09-02. A row may be `declared` only when BOTH hold: (a)
nothing in the tree deploys it, so the three derivations structurally cannot produce it — grep
either string across the whole tree at HEAD and you get zero files; AND (b) a live monitor for it
already exists. (b) is the half that stops `declared` decaying into the hand-typed list this
file was built to replace: it can only ever RECORD a monitor that is already there, never
invent a monitoring obligation nobody accepted.
🔴 notHostnamesAtAll: A HEARTBEAT MONITOR HAS NO HOSTNAME AND THEREFORE GETS NO ROW HERE. That is a rule, not an
oversight. Monitors 6 (`Laptop daily backup`), 16 (`GlitchTip backup chain`) and 19 (`Supabase
backup chain`) are type Heartbeat: they carry no url at all, and what they assert is that a POST
ARRIVED — not that a host answered. tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs prints each of them as `not
filed under any hostname in the register` on every scheduled run, correctly. Filing one under a
hostname would make this file say that something watches that host, which is the one claim it
THEY ARE STILL DECLARED, AND THEIR DISAPPEARANCE STILL FAILS A GUARD — in
tooling/ops/alarm-chains.json → expectedMonitors, which is keyed by monitor id and asks nothing
about hostnames. 📌 On 2026-09-03 monitor 19 was added THERE and deliberately not here, while
monitors 17 and 18 — found in the same sweep, live and undeclared since 2026-09-02 — became rows
here, because they are hostname monitors and 19 is not. Twelve monitors were live; nine were
declared; a canary naming nine of twelve cannot notice the other three being deleted.

closedGap.why: The monitor was type `Ping` — it proves a socket opened and nothing else. A Cloudflare Pages project serving a 500, an edge error page or a blank shell answers a ping, so this check was green over precisely the failure it existed to catch. tooling/ops/status.mjs named it on the day it landed and tooling/ops/register.json's `_deploySmokeExemptions` restated it, because this host has no deploy job to probe from and O-2's external prober is its whole coverage.
closedGap.howItWasClosed: Converted on the live instance via the GlitchTip API (PUT /api/0/organizations/nikatru/monitors/4/) and read back: monitorType GET, expectedStatus 200, everything else — url, interval 60s, timeout, confirmationThreshold, project — re-sent unchanged and diffed after, because PUT is a full replace. The save triggered an off-cadence check at 2026-08-10T19:22:21.660Z UTC which came back up in 32 ms.
closedGap.note: ✅ THE BODY LIMB IS CLOSED TOO — decided 2026-08-11, where this line used to park it as a separate decision. expectedBody is <link rel="canonical" href="https://nikatru.com/">, which is sites/nikatru/index.html line 8, read back off the LIVE page the same day: GET https://nikatru.com/ answered 200 with 32887 UTF-8 bytes, exactly the byte length of that file at HEAD — this page has no mailto, so Cloudflare's email obfuscation does not rewrite it, unlike monitor 5's host. WHY A DEPLOY CANNOT BREAK IT: it is not copy, not a hash and not a build id — copy edits move titles and prose, never the canonical URL — and it cannot be deleted quietly, because tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs DERIVES this hostname from this very tag (its siteCanonicals limb); delete or retarget it and nikatru.com stops being a derived hostname, this row becomes a dead row, and that guard's no-dead-rows limb fails the build. ⚠️ A mere REFORMAT of the tag is the one drift that guard does NOT catch — its regex tolerates whitespace and single quotes, the monitor's match is exact — so reformatting this tag is itself a two-file change. WHY AN OUTAGE DOES BREAK IT: the 404 this Pages project actually serves carries no canonical tag at all (measured: GET /__no_such_page__ → 404, a 3448-byte body, string absent), nor do Cloudflare's edge error pages, and an empty or wrong deploy serves that same 404. The tag is also HOST-SPECIFIC, so a deploy cross-wired between these two near-identical Pages projects fails it — measured: rajasekarselvam.com's canonical is absent from this body.

closedGap.why: Same defect and the same reason as nikatru.com: a `Ping` on a Pages host is green while the page behind it is a 500 or an empty shell, and this host's only coverage is O-2's external prober.
closedGap.howItWasClosed: PUT /api/0/organizations/nikatru/monitors/5/ with every existing value re-sent and only monitorType and expectedStatus changed; read back as GET / 200. The save's off-cadence check at 2026-08-10T19:22:22.230Z UTC came back up in 64 ms.
closedGap.note: ✅ CLOSED THE SAME WAY AND ON THE SAME DAY as monitor 4: expectedBody is <link rel="canonical" href="https://rajasekarselvam.com/">, which is sites/rajasekarselvam/index.html line 8, present in the live 200 body and absent from this project's 404 (measured: GET /__no_such_page__ → 404, a 3383-byte body, no canonical tag anywhere in it). 🔴 AND THIS HOST IS THE ONE THAT PROVES THE STRING HAD TO BE CHOSEN FOR EDGE-TRANSFORM SURVIVAL RATHER THAN FOR PRESENCE IN THE REPO — THE SERVED HTML IS NOT THE FILE AT HEAD. Cloudflare's Email Address Obfuscation rewrites this page: measured 2026-08-11, live line 277 serves /cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#… where the file says mailto:support@nikatru.com, and an /cdn-cgi/scripts/…/email-decode.min.js tag is injected ahead of the JSON-LD block at live line 291, so the live body is 22191 bytes against the file's 21948 across the same 377 lines, stable over three fetches. A body string taken from that region would be asserting about Cloudflare's rewrite rather than about this site. The canonical sits at head line 8, ahead of every transform, byte-identical in both. 📌 GENERALISABLE: a monitor's expectedBody must be read from the SERVED response, never from the file in the tree — this host serves 243 bytes that no commit contains.

hosts.what: the flagship app's web build — the only shipping client today

closedGap.why: The sharpest of the three. This is the only shipping client, it is a Flutter web build, and a Ping is green whenever the door opens — including when `flutter_bootstrap.js` is missing and the page renders nothing at all.
closedGap.howItWasClosed: PUT /api/0/organizations/nikatru/monitors/3/ with every existing value re-sent and only monitorType and expectedStatus changed; read back as GET / 200. The save's off-cadence check at 2026-08-10T19:22:21.062Z UTC came back up in 42 ms.
closedGap.note: ⚠️ THE BODY LIMB IS NOW ASSERTED AND IT STILL DOES NOT PROVE THE APP BOOTS — read the second half of this note before trusting the first. expectedBody is <base href="/">, measured live 2026-08-11: GET https://subly.nikatru.com/ → 200, 772 UTF-8 bytes. It was chosen over the <title> and over flutter_bootstrap.js because it is the ONE byte sequence in the served shell that exists only if a real flutter build web ran — the source template apps/subly/web/index.html carries the literal <base href="$FLUTTER_BASE_HREF">, and $FLUTTER_BASE_HREF does not appear in the live body at all. So it catches an edge error page, an empty or wrong Pages project, and a deploy of the SOURCE directory instead of build/web; and tooling/ci/test/smoke-web-artifact.test.mjs already records a failing case for this exact string — <base href="/"> rewritten to /nope/ → exit 1 naming four 404s, run against a real flutter build web. 🔴 WHAT IT STILL CANNOT SEE, AND NO GET EVER WILL: this shell is a loader and a monitor runs no JavaScript, so flutter_bootstrap.js 404ing, main() throwing, or the first frame never rasterizing ALL still answer 200 with this exact body. That is also precisely why flutter_bootstrap.js was REJECTED as the string — it is present in the shell exactly when the file it names is missing, so it would read as coverage of the failure it cannot see. The did-it-boot half stays with the nightly e2e and with tooling/smoke/smoke-web-artifact.mjs's flutter-first-frame signal. Note also that GET /__no_such_page__ on this host returns 200 with this same shell (SPA fallback, measured), so this body says nothing about routing either.

🔴 openBodyGap.why: MONITOR 2 STAYS GREEN THROUGH EVERY FAULT PR #384 MADE DETECTABLE — it asserts `expectedStatus` 200 and NO body, while `/v1/health` deliberately answers 200 even when `ok` is false — so the matcher this row will carry, "ok":true, is knowingly NOT declared in `monitor` above until the live GlitchTip PUT lands, because tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs compares DECLARED bodies only and a register-only assertion makes it exit 1 inside the SCHEDULED `glitchtip` job at .github/workflows/ops-watch.yml:456, which opens the portfolio's never-auto-closed durable alert issue.
🔴 openBodyGap.measuredNotAssumed: Reconciled 2026-08-26 against a local stand-in serving monitor 2 with an empty live `expectedBody` and every other monitor as recorded: verify-monitors.mjs printed six `ok` rows, then `✗ api.nikatru.com — monitor id 2 declares expectedBody ... and the live monitor carries (none)`, and exited 1. That exit 1 is what reaches the `alert` job. No live instance was contacted and nothing was authenticated to produce this.
🔴 openBodyGap.soThisRowIsNotAWaiver: The row declares no `expectedBody`, so it claims no coverage it does not have; this block states the missing coverage rather than dropping it. Same discipline as `monitor: null` elsewhere in this file — written down and printed, not silenced, and not failing a build over work that is not a change to this repository.
🔴 openBodyGap.⚠️ theReconcileIsNotSILENCED: Nothing was added to an ignore list and no check was weakened. The declared-body limb is DECLARED-ONLY by design (tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs:179-190) precisely so a row may decline to assert; withdrawing the claim USES that design rather than blunting it, and the limb still guards monitors 3, 4, 5, 11 and 12 on every scheduled run. The moment the PUT lands and `expectedBody` returns to `monitor` above, it guards this row too.

theLiveChangeThatClosesThis.whyOwner: A write to a live third-party instance, not a repository change. ⚠️ AND NOTE THIS FILE'S OWN WARNING at `🔴 whyItStayedOpen` under platform.nikatru.com: 'owner action' here is a claim needing evidence, not a category — the GlitchTip API demonstrably takes GLITCHTIP_TOKEN and mutates monitors. What gates THIS one is blast radius, not capability: tooling/channel-register.json:813 records that on 2026-08-11 echoing a monitor's own representation back through this full-replace PUT detached all nine monitors from their projects — from every alert recipient — under nine consecutive HTTP 200s ([ADR 043], amended).
theLiveChangeThatClosesThis.🔴 fullReplace: PUT IS A FULL REPLACE. Re-send every existing field unchanged alongside this one — name, url, monitorType, expectedStatus, interval, timeout, confirmationThreshold AND project — exactly as monitors 3, 4 and 5 were converted on 2026-08-11, then diff the read-back. Omitting `project` is what silently disarms the alert chain under a 200.
theLiveChangeThatClosesThis.readBackWith: GLITCHTIP_TOKEN=… node tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs — exit 0 is the proof. Then, in ONE commit, delete this whole `🔴 openBodyGap` block and restore the `expectedBody` field to the `monitor` object above with the value recorded here.
theLiveChangeThatClosesThis.matcherProvenance: The value above is byte-for-byte identical to monitor 11's live, verified string on the same `/v1/health` shape — codepoints [34,111,107,34,58,116,114,117,101] for both, nine characters, NO space after the colon. A near-miss such as a space after the colon would be silently permissive, which is this wave's entire subject.

📌 mustLandWithTheLiveChange: services/subly-api/test/health.test.ts (branch fix/health-that-can-fail, PR #384) — asserts monitor 2's BODY-LESS state as a LIVE FACT, and goes stale the moment the PUT lands.
services/subly-api/src/index.ts — restates the same claim in the `/v1/health` header comment, and goes stale with it.

Both going stale is BY DESIGN — the note deletes itself when the gap closes — but they must land together with the PUT, or the tree asserts two contradictory things about one live monitor. Neither file belongs to the writer of this register.

hosts.what: the crash sink and the monitor host itself
hosts.why: No wrangler.jsonc, app row or site canonical names it: it is not something this repo deploys, it is the thing watching what this repo deploys. Declared here so 'who watches the watcher' is at least askable.

hosts.what: the shared platform Worker — POST /v1/events and POST /v1/consent, the whole analytics and DPDP consent rail for every app in the portfolio

closedGap.why: Bound as a custom domain in services/platform/wrangler.jsonc since the Worker shipped and unmonitored for three days. This was the highest-consequence unwatched host in the tree: if it stops answering, every stamped app's events queue locally and nothing anywhere goes red.
closedGap.howItWasClosed: Created on the live GlitchTip instance via its API, then exercised: the production perform_checks task ran a real check against https://platform.nikatru.com/v1/health and it came back up (32 ms).
closedGap.🔴 whyItStayedOpen: The action line said 'An owner action on the GlitchTip instance, not a repository change.' That was WRONG, and it parked the tree's highest-consequence gap for three days. The GlitchTip API takes the vault token and creates monitors; an agent did exactly that twice on 2026-08-05 while proving the alert chain. Same shape as the 'the agent cannot SSH out' claim that survived in four files and parked an entire hardening backlog: A DOCUMENTED LIMIT THAT NOBODY PROBED. Probe before inheriting.
closedGap.note: GET on / returns 404 for this Worker — it only answers its declared routes — so a Ping monitor on the bare host would have alarmed permanently. The monitor targets the real health route and asserts the body, not just the status: a Worker returning 200 with an error payload is exactly the failure a status-only check cannot see.

hosts.what: the shared platform Worker's config surface — GET /config/:app, the pre-consent launch fetch every client makes

closedGap.why: Same wrangler.jsonc, same omission. It is the FIRST request a launching app makes, so its failure is a launch failure rather than a degraded feature.
closedGap.howItWasClosed: Created via the GlitchTip API and exercised with the production perform_checks task against https://config.nikatru.com/config/subly — up, 36 ms.
closedGap.note: ⚠️ THE MONITORED PATH NAMES ONE APP. `/config/:app` is per-app, so a monitor has to pick one, and `subly` is the only shipping client today. When a second app ships, this checks that the config surface ANSWERS, not that the second app's config exists — and nothing here will say so. Revisit when the portfolio grows past one client.

hosts.what: the self-hosted Supabase auth surface — GoTrue behind an Envoy gateway, and the sign-in path for the only shipping client
hosts.why: Nothing in this tree deploys it or names it: no wrangler.jsonc route, no catalog/apps.json field, no site canonical, and a grep for the string across the whole tree at HEAD returns zero files. It is the self-hosted Supabase stack named by SUPABASE_SELFHOST_API_URL in the local vault, not anything this factory deploys. ⚠️ WHICH BOX SERVES IT IS NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS REPOSITORY, and it is not inferred here: the 401 below was measured on Box A's gateway log, while GlitchTip moved to Box B on the same day these monitors appeared, and 'they arrived together' is not evidence that they run together. It is declared because a live hostname monitor already watches it — and because until 2026-09-03 that monitor appeared in NO declaration in this repository, so nothing here could say it existed, let alone that it was broken.

closedGap.why: 🔴 IT WAS A MONITOR THAT COULD NOT FAIL — the sharpest defect in this file's history, because it is the one that reads as coverage on every surface. From its creation on 2026-09-02 it polled GET /auth/v1/health with `expectedStatus: 401`, and 401 is what that path returns whether GoTrue is healthy, wedged or gone: the Envoy gateway rejects the request for a missing apikey BEFORE it reaches the auth service. Measured 2026-09-03 on the gateway's own request log (Box A): 1,464 of the last 2,000 requests to that path were 401. It asserted the gateway's own refusal, so it was green over exactly the failure it was named for.
closedGap.🔴 theProofThatTheRequestNeverReachedGoTr: Measured from outside, 2026-09-03, and it is a single header. The 200 on /auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json carries `x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 0` — an upstream produced it. The 401 on /auth/v1/health carries NO such header at all — the gateway produced it alone, and nothing behind the gateway was ever consulted. That header is the difference between 'the auth service answered' and 'the door said no', and no status code could have told them apart.
closedGap.howItWasClosed: PUT /api/0/organizations/nikatru/monitors/17/. ⚠️ PATCH DOES NOT EXIST ON THIS ENDPOINT — measured, not assumed: OPTIONS returns 405 with `allow: DELETE, GET, PUT`, so the full-replace PUT is the only route and the 2026-08-11 discipline is mandatory. Every field was re-sent unchanged with `project: "1"` included, and the read-back was diffed field by field against the read-before: exactly three changed — url /auth/v1/health → /auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json, expectedStatus 401 → 200, expectedBody "" → "\"keys\"" — and projectID/projectName stayed "1"/subly, which is the field whose silent loss detached all nine monitors from their alert recipients under nine HTTP 200s on 2026-08-11 (tooling/channel-register.json:813). The save's off-cadence check at 2026-09-03T10:03:35.371Z UTC came back up in 34 ms.
closedGap.whyThisPathAndNotTheAlternatives: Every candidate was fetched live before one was chosen. /auth/v1/health, /auth/v1/settings, /auth/v1/user, /auth/v1/sso, /auth/v1/logout, /auth/v1/factors and /auth/v1/ all answer 401 from the gateway. /auth/v1/verify answers 400 from GoTrue itself — real evidence of life, but a register that asserts 400 is the healthy state is a register nobody can read. /auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json answers 200 with {"keys":[]}, from the upstream, with no apikey at all. THE REJECTED OPTION WAS CHANGING expectedStatus TO 401: it would have made the monitor assert today's reality, and it still could not have told a healthy GoTrue from a dead one — which is the entire defect, restated as a declaration. THE OTHER REJECTED OPTION was putting an apikey on the monitor URL: it works, and it would put a key in a monitor URL and in this PUBLIC file, to be rotated in two places forever.
closedGap.note: ⚠️ WHAT IT STILL CANNOT SEE, stated so the green is read correctly. JWKS is a static handler: a 200 proves GoTrue's process is up and serving, NOT that it can reach Postgres or issue a token, so a database-side auth outage answers this check 200 all day. The did-it-actually-sign-in half is not in GlitchTip at all. The body matcher is "keys" — six characters, codepoints [34,107,101,121,115,34], no space — and it holds whether the key set is empty (it is today, HS256) or populated. ⚠️ AND ONE CACHING CAVEAT, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: the response carries `Cache-Control: public, max-age=600`, so were a Cloudflare cache rule ever to start caching it, this monitor could read a stale 200 for up to ten minutes after GoTrue died. Three consecutive fetches on 2026-09-03 all returned `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` — not cached today. The day that reads HIT, this monitor has gone soft and this row has to say so.

hosts.what: the self-hosted Supabase Studio — the admin console for the same self-hosted Supabase stack as api-auth.nikatru.com, published to the internet behind Cloudflare Access
hosts.why: The same rule as api-auth.nikatru.com, and the same two facts: nothing in this tree deploys it or names it, and a live hostname monitor (id 18) has watched it since 2026-09-02 while appearing in no declaration here until 2026-09-03.
🔴 whatThisMonitorIsForAndWhatItIsNot: READ THE MATCHER BEFORE READING THE GREEN. `Cloudflare Access` is the text of the interstitial
LOGIN page. So this monitor is green when an anonymous request to the admin console is STOPPED
by the Access gate, and it goes red if the gate is removed or bypassed and Studio starts
answering the internet directly. It watches an exposure, not an uptime.
⚠️ IT THEREFORE SAYS NOTHING ABOUT STUDIO ITSELF. Access renders its login page whether the
console behind it is healthy, stopped or deleted, so a dead Studio is green here. That is NOT
monitor 17's defect — this check can fail, and it fails on the thing it is named for — but a
reader who takes this row as 'the admin console is up' is reading a claim it does not make.
Recorded rather than fixed: asserting Studio's liveness needs a credential, and a credential
in a monitor is a way in.

spof: 🔴 EVERY MONITOR ABOVE RUNS INSIDE GLITCHTIP ON ONE BOX, including monitor id 1,
which watches glitchtip.nikatru.com. So does the alert path (Resend SMTP). If that box is down,
every check is down and the notification that would say so is down with it — the failure is
indistinguishable from everything being healthy.
⚠️ WHICH BOX THAT IS CHANGED ON 2026-09-02. THE SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE DID NOT. Until
2026-09-03 the paragraph above read 'EVERY MONITOR ABOVE RUNS INSIDE GLITCHTIP ON ONE ORACLE
CLOUD BOX'. That was stale: GlitchTip, its monitors, its alert evaluation and its backup chain
moved to the Hostinger box (Box B) on 2026-09-02 — recorded in tooling/ops/alarm-chains.json →
_expectedMonitorsWhy, whose whole subject is the 46-hour freeze that move caused, and in
tooling/ops/register.json:1185, where monitor 16 was renamed for the same reason on the same
day. The old sentence is NAMED here rather than quietly overwritten, because the correction is
one word and nothing else: one box became a different box, the count is still ONE, and E-9b is
exactly as open today as it was on 2026-08-03. A reader who remembers 'Oracle' has to be able to
see that the sentence was corrected — not that the problem was solved.
